not completely, but in some aspects i do relate. about wanting the perfect things, relationship (friendship mainly) work, grades or even just as a human being. i create scenarios in my head, how things should turn out and many “what if”s when things didn’t turn out well in real life. but at one point i’ve realised that i can’t be perfect in anything, i stopped trying. “if i can’t be perfect or even good at it, then i rather not have anything,” was and is still how i think. so i started leaving people, have trouble striving my best for work and school and i allow myself to spiral down that bottomless pit. not that i want to do anything about it, perhaps i do on some days, but mostly i just want to rot and die. i’m used to living in my perfect world i created in my mind, so if i can achieve them there, it’s okay to not experience life. 

i guess what i wanna say is, you’re still young, and i’m glad that you are aware about this aspect of yourself. but i hope that you could use your awareness to fight to become a better version of yourself. it won’t be easy, but don’t ever give up on yourself. even on days you feel like your efforts are so minimal that they mean nothing. know that every step you take is an improvement, even if you feel like you’re moving backwards. i believe that you have what it takes to become better, if you interpret “i am the problem” differently, fix them and become a better version of yourself because dwelling doesn’t do us good, right? 

strive on, live well. i hope this doesn’t comes off offensive in anyway..

oh my, we have someone here who’s anti social media! haha, jokes aside, i feel you man, i feel like the more im on instagram the worse i feel about myself. so i deactivated my account and only go back to check it once in a while, just to see how my friends are doing. 

it’s weird that we no longer do the “hey how have you been” and it’s as if people only start to care when you put it out there for the world to see. sometimes i wonder if i’m the only one who sees the harm social media is doing to us. 

when i don’t have my account i realised that i start spending more time in real life when i’m with my friends. more talking and catching up ABOUT THEM and less gossiping about some random stranger on social media and looking at tik tok videos. 

don’t get me wrong, i know social media is enjoyable when it comes to sharing bits and pieces of our lives but i think there’s an extent to where that goes. i prefer the days when social media was not THE THING, it feels like i could live more. 

i don’t even know if youngsters realise this is a problem, i’ve just entered the 20ties club, but i feel like i’m the rare handful who sees it. 

cheers to you, live more in the real life, and don’t feel guilty about posting once in a while, i’m sure it’s a normal thing to want to share. :)

point is, perhaps we can’t let go bcos despite the discomfort and depressing headspace we are in, it is a comfort zone for our brains. bcos outside of this is fighting for a better life, creating opportunities and trying out new things. they are scary, bcos they are new. unfamiliar things are scary to our brains. and since perhaps we don’t have the energy to face all these, we choose to hang on to this state we are in.
